- **Output:** `/Users/dev/terminal-bench/cwe-bench/stacking/out/screener/23616.json`. I read every cited line before writing it.
- **Trust decision:** the client decides how big an inbound broker frame may be. Both transport readers (blocking socket and Netty) keep a 64 MiB limit set when they are created, and it is never lowered to the frame_max agreed during connection setup (`src/main/java/com/rabbitmq/client/impl/AMQConnection.java:428-431`).
- **`pattern_fit`: A, and a weak one.** Only two O8 routes exist, both easy to dismiss: oversized frames during the handshake, before frame_max is agreed, and the Netty decoder buffering a whole oversized frame before rejecting it. The only real how-type room is the size boundary: a frame of exactly frame_max must pass, frame_max = 0 means no cap, and a smaller user limit must stay.
- **Strongest lever:** the Netty transport's own size check (`src/main/java/com/rabbitmq/client/impl/NettyFrameHandlerFactory.java:544`). Netty is off by default and its `readFrame()` throws, so a solver who fixes `Frame.readFrom` can argue the job is done. It is in the same package and shares an error message with `Frame.readFrom`, so one search finds it.
- **Biggest red flag:** no formal O12 flag applies. The practical risk is the build: it needs the separate `rabbitmq_codegen` repo, which is not in the pinned tree. I did not check whether it can be vendored for offline use, and repo size was not measured.
